_comment: The contract between the Java server-KPI evaluator and the report's client-side mirror (M6).
ServerParityTest runs it in Java; server-parity.test.js and server-parity.spec.ts are to run
the same cases in node and in a real report. Neither side owns the definition of a reducer,
a tolerance, the window, requiresLoad or divideBy: this file does. A case only one side passes
is the bug the file exists to catch. Add a case whenever either side gains behaviour.
`payload` is a literal server-metrics.json (read through the same bean the generator reads).
`samplers` and `clientRules` build the client gate requiresLoad/divideBy resolve against,
through the client evaluator. `config` per case overrides the block's run-level settings.
Expected `actual` values are compared to 1e-6; `reason` is a substring of the detail.
`kpi` is the RAW file entry - one server assert, an element of serverMetrics.asserts (the key
keeps its internal name; D25 renamed only what a user writes): every runner puts it in a block's
`asserts` and through its production parser (Java: ServerMetricsMapper), so a shape one parser
refuses and the other reads is a failing case.
`expect.id` is the id the assert is judged under - the derived one when the file names none.
`expect.warnings`, when present, is the exact list of WARNING sentences KpiUsability raises for
the assert (Java: its WARNING findings; the browser: what the editor and a drag show) - they
decide nothing, so only the sentence can drift, and it is the sentence a reader acts on.
`documentCases` judge several asserts in one block (`asserts`, the file's own key), for what
only a set can show (shared ids). Their `warnings`, when present, is the exact, ordered list of
WARNING findings the document raises, as {id, message} (Java: every WARNING in findings(); the
browser: the live duplicate-id findings, then each assert's own warnings). Their `findings`, when
present, is the exact, ordered list of EVERY finding the document raises, ERRORs and WARNINGs, as
{severity, id, message} (Java: ServerGateEvaluation.findings(), in its phases - the mapper's, then
KpiUsability's per assert, then the payload's, then the evaluator's run-time refusals, each said
once per assert; the browser: the live findings list, SF18). A document case's `block`, when present,
adds or replaces block keys beside its components and asserts (environments, defaultEnv, collection).
`blockCases` are what a BLOCK says beside its asserts: each key of `block` replaces the block's
own (a `components` there replaces every declared component), `expect.problems` is the exact, ordered
list of config-level ERROR sentences the mapper records under serverMetrics (Java:
ServerMetricsConfig.problems() filed under serverMetrics; the browser: blockProblems),
`expect.componentProblems` (absent means none) the same for the components, as {id, message} with the
finding's id - serverMetrics.components.<id> (the browser: componentProblems) - and `expect.ids` the
asserts that still map beside them.
`components` is the block's declared components, as a user writes them, for every case: `c` is
custom (every assert writes its own query) and `db` is postgres (asserts name a catalogue metric,
which brings its query, unit and reducer). A case (or a document case) may carry its own
`components`, merged over those by id. Every assert names a component; there are no sources in
the file any more (C8): the payload's one source is the collection's, id `metrics`, and every
series is keyed by it and by the query the assert resolved to. A gate case cannot name a case
that carries its own `components` or `config`.
`expect.detail`, when present, is the WHOLE detail sentence, compared for equality - for the
sentences whose every character is part of the contract (numbers above all: a value is written
as Java writes it on both sides - a quoted value or a reducer key in Double.toString's E notation
below 1e-3 and from 1e7, a band in plain digits - every digit of an integral one below 2^63, and
Double.toString's shortest digits written out for any other (L12) - and a value read from the file
by its value, never its literal).
`invisibleEnds.ranges` is the class of characters the INVISIBLE_PADDING WARNING names at a query's
end (F8): each side holds its own copy as a range table, and ServerParityTest and server-parity.test.js
check that copy against this one for every code point (server-parity.spec.ts: each range's edges
and one either side), so neither side's Unicode tables decide what the WARNING says.

samplers._comment: R2-1: a throughput just under a load rule's limit. round2 would put it ON the limit (12.5), which is where the page used to judge it.
samplers.name: GET /edge

clientRules._comment: R1-3: no id. Java derives target.slug()-metric = run-throughput; the mirror must too.
R2-3: an explicit null, as the page's annotationsDocument serialises an id-less rule. Derived: get-api-products-throughput.
C-3: Java canonicalises the metric before asking whether it is throughput.
C38: a load target with six digits. Its FAILED sentence quotes the band, and the page wrote it with the reader's grouping separator (100,000) where Java writes 100000.
M7d X: a load target Java wrote in E notation (Double.toString from 1e7), where the page wrote 12345678.5. L12: a band is written in plain digits, so both write 12345678.5.
M7d X: a load target Java wrote in E notation (Double.toString below 1e-3), FAILed by GET /idle's 0 req/s, where the page wrote 0.0005. L12: a band is written in plain digits, so both write 0.0005.

Q19 (item 3): a load rule whose fail band covers its warn band (a WARNING, still judged), so GET /edge's 12.496 FAILs lt 13 beside warn lt 12.5. The quoted measurement counts the warn band too: the fail band alone would write 12.50, on the warn band it crossed.

L13: one 'worst'. Two FAILs of one load rule: GET /api/products' 12.5 first, then GET /idle's 0, further past the downward band. RuleResult.worstJudged() and the mirror's worstJudged both name the furthest past it, not the first.

reasonPhrases._comment: NotJudged.phrase() and WIR.status.REASON_PHRASE, word for word: the load-rule sentences are built from them on both sides.
reasonPhrases.NO_VALUE: could not be measured in this run
reasonPhrases.LOW_COVERAGE: was collected below the coverage floor
reasonPhrases.LOAD_NOT_ACHIEVED: was not judged because the load it depends on was not established

reasonCountKeys._comment: A1-9: NotJudged.countKey() and WIR.status.REASON_KEY - the key a reason is counted under in gate.notJudged on both sides.

_comment: F8 (Q2): the characters a query may not start or end with without a WARNING - KpiUsability.isInvisible
and the page's isInvisibleCodePoint, which each hold this table as their own copy. It is Unicode's
White_Space, plus every Default_Ignorable_Code_Point, plus DEL and the C1 controls, minus everything
at or below U+0020, which String.trim (and the page's javaTrim) has already taken off both ends.
Written out rather than derived on either side: the JVM's and the browser's Unicode tables move
between versions (U+180E was a space separator until Unicode 6.3, a format character since), and a
class each side computes from its own tables is two classes. Maximal ranges, ascending, inclusive,
as hex code points: 007F-00A0 is DEL, the C1 controls and the no-break space together.
A visible character can end in one of them - an emoji in its emoji presentation ends in U+FE0F, a
subdivision flag in U+E007F - and the WARNING names that one too: the file alone cannot tell padding
from presentation, and a WARNING decides nothing (Q6). Validate query and wir-collect, which hold
what came back, say nothing of it for a series that returned points.
`loneSurrogates` reads an end as Java's codePointAt and codePointBefore do: a high half followed by
a low half is one code point, and any other half is itself, which no range lists. Each case is its
UTF-16 units in hex, so no half has to be written as an escape here, and `warning` is the whole
sentence, or null for none.

loneSurrogates.name: a high half at the start that no low half follows is not joined to what follows it (joined to U+E000 it would read U+E0400, inside the tag block)
a no-break space after a high half is not joined to it, so the end is the no-break space
loneSurrogates.warning: the query has an invisible character at its end (U+00A0) that is not trimmed like a plain space, so no series will match it — delete it

loneSurrogates.name: a low half at the start, with no high half before it, is itself
a high half at the end, with no low half after it, is itself
a pair at the start is one code point, the tag space

_comment: M7d X (review:C, review:F): every number a refusal or a warning prints is written as Java
writes it. ServerMetricsMapper.describe quotes a value by its VALUE (an integral one below
1e15 as a long, anything else as Double.toString); Reducer.key writes Durations.trim - a
long's digits for an integral value (saturating, as (long) does), else Double.toString,
whose E notation starts below 1e-3 and at 1e7. The mirror printed String(d): 1e-7 where Java
wrote 1.0E-7, 12345678.5 where it wrote 1.23456785E7.
L12: Predicate.describe writes a band in plain digits - every digit of an integral band below
2^63, and Double.toString's shortest digits for any other (an integral one from 2^63 included,
so 1e23 is 100000000000000000000000), never saturated and never in E notation. It wrote
Durations.trim too, so a band of 0.0005 read 5.0E-4 and one of 1e21 read 9223372036854775807.
